cards.explanation: The answer is a yoke, made out of leather straps. The LORD tells Jeremiah to make it for himself and put it on his neck (Jeremiah 27:2). He doesn't just give him words, friends. He gives him something to make and wear. I think that's an outfit people would stop and ask about.

The answer is their kings back home. The envoys have come to Jerusalem, so the LORD tells Jeremiah to send word through them. Verse 4 says it's a message for them to relay to their masters. It's a delivery with built-in delivery guys, and the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon are the ones the word is for.

The answer is whoever He pleases. God says, “…I give it to whom I please.” He made the earth, so the giving is His to do (Jeremiah 27:5). Nobody wins it by flexing and nobody gets it by being quick. It's His land, and He decides who gets it.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. God says He has placed all these lands under his authority (Jeremiah 27:6). That's a lot of lands for one man to be put over, friends. I think that man needs a very big calendar.

The answer is False. God says the nations will serve Nebuchadnezzar and his son and grandson, until the time of his own land comes (Jeremiah 27:7). After that, many nations and great kings will enslave him. Even the top spot comes with an end date.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy one. God says any nation that won't serve Nebuchadnezzar or place its neck under his yoke will be punished by sword and famine and plague (Jeremiah 27:8). It goes on until He has destroyed that nation by his hand. This is the LORD speaking, and the warning is plain.

The answer is destroyed. God says He'll punish that nation until He has destroyed it by Nebuchadnezzar's hand (Jeremiah 27:8). It's a heavy line, and it shows how serious the warning is, friends. The yoke is the way out of it.

The answer is that they will not serve the king of Babylon. Every voice in that crowd is declaring it (Jeremiah 27:9). It sounds nice to hear, and I bet it was popular. But the LORD tells them not to listen. Same pitch from every direction doesn't make it true.

The answer is a lie. God says they prophesy a lie that will serve to remove their listeners from their land (Jeremiah 27:10). Then He says He will banish them and they will perish. A lie that sounds good is still a lie, friends, and this one costs people their home.

The answer is True. God says the nation that puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him will be left in its own land (Jeremiah 27:11). It will cultivate the land and live in it. After all that warning, here's the kind part: the yoke comes with a home.

The answer is live. Jeremiah tells Zedekiah and his people to put their necks under the yoke, serve, and live (Jeremiah 27:12). Right in the middle of a hard message is the word live, friends. I bet that's the word to hold on to.

The answer is False, and Jeremiah couldn't be plainer. He says do not listen to the words of the prophets who say you must not serve the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 27:14). He says they are prophesying a lie. Some advice you take. This one you leave alone.

The answer is sent. The LORD says He has not sent them, and yet they are prophesying falsely in His name (Jeremiah 27:15). They're using His name, but they're not on His errand, friends. Using the name isn't the same as being sent.

The answer is that the articles will be brought back very soon. That's what those prophets say: very soon now the articles will be brought back from Babylon (Jeremiah 27:16). Jeremiah passes on what the LORD says: they are prophesying a lie. That settles it.
The answer is ruin. Jeremiah says to serve the king of Babylon and live, and then he asks why this city should become a ruin (Jeremiah 27:17). The sentence right before it says serve and live.

The answer is that the articles still left stay put. That's the challenge, friends. If they're prophets and the word of the LORD is with them, let them plead that the articles remaining in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem not be taken to Babylon (Jeremiah 27:18). Jeremiah isn't asking them for more promises. He's asking them to plead for the things that are still there.

The answer is Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, a king of Judah. Nebuchadnezzar carried him into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon (Jeremiah 27:20). The pillars, the sea, the bases and the rest were left behind when that happened.

The answer is True. When Nebuchadnezzar carried Jeconiah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, he took along all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem (Jeremiah 27:20). It's a heavy part of the story, friends. Jeconiah didn't go alone.

The answer is Babylon. The LORD of Hosts says the articles that remain in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem will be carried there (Jeremiah 27:22). The prophets said the articles would be back very soon (Jeremiah 27:16). The LORD says they go to Babylon.

The answer is False, and this is the hopeful part. The LORD says the articles will remain in Babylon until the day He attends to them again (Jeremiah 27:22). Then He says, “Then I will bring them back and restore them to this place.” They go, but they don't stay lost.
